QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_14

question.text: Upon obtaining 75% investor approval for in-specie distribution of unliquidated investments, the AIF must arrange bids. What is the minimum value of bids required, and what happens if the bid threshold is not met?

answer.text: 10% of unliquidated value; if not met, the AIF must launch a Liquidation Scheme.
25% of unliquidated value; if the threshold is met, in-specie is at bid value; if not met, in-specie is at One Rupee.
50% of unliquidated value; if not met, SEBI directs forced sale to a QIB.
100% of unliquidated value; otherwise the assets cannot be distributed.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 12 (SEBI Second Amendment 2024), upon investor approval for in-specie distribution, the AIF must arrange bids for a MINIMUM of 25% of the value of unliquidated investments. If achieved, in-specie distribution happens at BID VALUE; if the 25% bid threshold is NOT achieved, in-specie happens at ONE RUPEE for performance-benchmarking purposes. Dissenters get full exit out of the 25% bid; any unsubscribed portion provides pro-rata exit to non-dissenters. The Trap: 10% and 50% are plausible but wrong thresholds. 100% is impossible by definition (if 100% could be sold, it would not be 'unliquidated'). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same 25% rule. Post-April 25, 2024, no NEW Liquidation Schemes can be launched, so that route (option A) is closed.
